label: input u/h/q/e/n/v in specific contexts (copy: next output a/r/o/c/k/f/j; original: after h/x/1/2/u/t)
explanation: Sparse unit (~1% of steps). Nearly all activation (96% of mass) happens when the input token is one of u, h, q, e, n, v; u alone accounts for 40% of the mass. But it is active on only ~5% of steps with those inputs, so the token is necessary and far from sufficient. In the copy phase, activity is enriched when the token about to be output is a, r, o, c, k, f or j (a is the strongest). The largest activations (up to max) are on the first copy steps where u/e is fed back and the next output is a. In the original phase, it is enriched when the previous input is h, x, 1, 2, u or t. Never active at t=0 or at the delimiter step. Rate rises with L. The combined predicate reaches dev F1 0.28 and mass recall 0.72; precision stays low (~0.18), so the remaining gating depends on hidden state I could not capture with simple history variables.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=u (+6.22), in_tok=h (+5.93), in_tok=q (+5.76), phase=2 & in_tok=n (+5.73), in_tok=v (+4.73), phase=2 & out_tok=a (+4.68). Lower it: prev_tok=a (-3.09), prev_tok=r (-2.50), prev3_tok=a (-2.44), prev2_tok=a (-2.35).
